## Our caring and compassionate veterinary care team!

Meet the Veterinarians & Team of Stonecrest Animal Medical Center in Huntington! We’re pleased to provide exceptional vet care for your pets!

​

Please call us at 304-525-1800 to speak to one of our caring veterinary staff members!

### Veterinarian / Owner

Image: Leigh Johnson.jpg

Dr. Leigh Johnson

Dr. Johnson was born and raised in Saint Albans, WV. She received her Bachelor of Science degree from West Virginia University, and went on to graduate from veterinary school at The Ohio State University. After school, she returned to WV, and practiced both large and small animal medicine for 3 years, before making the switch to small animal exclusive. She purchased Stonecrest Animal Medical Center, and Ceredo Kenova Animal Clinic in January 2016, and feels very fortunate to have become a part of such a fantastic team! Dr. Johnson enjoys all aspects of veterinary medicine, but has a special interest in internal medicine cases, auto-immune disorders, and chemotherapy.

### Chemotherapy

Image

Cancer is always a frightening condition, whether it is diagnosed in people or our furry family members. Fortunately at All Creatures, Dr. Streit and Dr. Hughes have many years of experience in successfully treating cancer in pets. Our clinic is equipped with the most advanced laboratory equipment available in order to make a proper diagnosis of the disease.

Once the illness has been properly identified, our doctors use only the safest and most effective medications to treat your pet. Finally, pain medication is administered as needed in order to keep them as comfortable as possible during the treatment process.

While cancer is still a difficult disease, the caring doctors and staff at All Creatures make it much easier on your furry family member as well as you. All dogs and cats over the age of five years of age should have a physical exam and blood work run to diagnose any disease, but especially cancer, as soon as possible.

Early diagnosis and treatment can often make cancer more manageable and treatable for pets. If your furry family member does not have a current veterinarian or is five years of age or greater, contact the compassionate team at All Creatures and schedule an appointment today!

# Local Family’s Chemo Tote Ministry Brings Comfort, Faith, and Support to Patients Across the Community

March 24, 2026

Image

For Immediate Release
March 24, 2026

Local Family’s Chemo Tote Ministry Brings Comfort, Faith, and Support to Patients Across the Community

BUCKHANNON, W.Va. — At WVU Medicine St. Joseph’s Hospital, compassionate care extends far beyond clinical treatment - and thanks to one local family’s ministry, cancer patients are receiving comfort, encouragement, and reminders that they are not alone.

Jessica Johnson and her children began assembling “chemo totes” in 2019 after losing her mother, Diana, to breast cancer following a courageous four-year battle. What started as a deeply personal act of love has grown into a community-wide outreach that has delivered more than 700 totes to patients across north-central West Virginia.

Dr. Mallett and the oncology team work together to lengthen and preserve the quality of life for dogs and cats with cancer. Our state-of-the-art, USP 800-compliant oncology suite is optimized for the safety and comfort of our patients.

## Services Offered

At Virginia Veterinary Specialty & Emergency, we offer the following cancer treatment services:

  * Comprehensive consultation and examination
  * Diagnostic tests for cancer staging and monitoring
  * Follow-up and recheck exams
  * Traditional chemotherapy
  * Targeted chemotherapy
  * Immunotherapy (including the ONCEPT® melanoma vaccine)
  * Coordination for oncologic surgery
  * Basic discussion and external referral for radiation therapy
  * Management of treatment and disease-related side effects/symptoms
  * Palliative care recommendations

We understand that you and your pet are going through a difficult time, and we are here for you. To best serve our patients, the oncology department sees patients by appointment only. We also require a definitive cancer diagnosis, and a referral from a current, local primary care veterinarian.

For more information about veterinary oncology, please visit:

  * The American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine, Oncology
  * The Veterinary Cancer Society


## Oncology Department Hours at VVSE

The oncology team is in the office Monday through Thursday from 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. We welcome you to give us a call at (434) 202-2987 if you have a question or would like to schedule an appointment. Please note that we do not offer remote cancer management or telemedicine services at this time.

Call: (434) 202-2987

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Will chemotherapy make my pet sick?

A: Unlike human oncology, veterinary chemotherapy is typically administered at lower doses to minimize side effects. Most pets tolerate treatment very well and maintain a good quality of life. If side effects occur, they are usually mild and manageable.

Q: How much does oncology treatment cost?

A: Costs vary depending on diagnostics, treatment plan, and duration of care. After evaluating your pet, we provide a detailed treatment estimate and discuss available options.

Q: How do I schedule an oncology consultation?

A: You can contact our hospital directly to schedule a consultation. Our team will guide you through the next steps and help gather any medical records needed before your visit.

Q: What is the prognosis for my pet?

A: Prognosis depends on the cancer type, stage, and your pet’s overall health. During your visit, we will discuss realistic expectations, treatment goals, and likely outcomes so you can make informed decisions.

Through direct financial assistance and referrals to other programs, the Commission assisted 35

hospital financial counselors, regional community action agencies, hotels with discounts for medical 
treatment, and local cancer assistance programs. Prescription drug discounts and online medical co-
payment assistance were also utilized. By working with these partners and available resources, the 
Commission leverages additional funds for client assistance services.  
 
A key objective of the Commission is to leverage scarce resources for maximum benefit.  An example of 
leveraging can be seen in the Commission’s historical data: for every dollar billed to the Commission for

transplants and endocrine therapy. 
9. Palliative Procedures 
• This identifies any care provided in an effort to palliate or alleviate 
symptoms. Palliative care is performed to relieve symptoms and 
may include surgery, radiation therapy, systemic therapy 
(chemotherapy, hormone therapy, or other systemic drugs), and/or 
other pain management therapy. 
10. Other Therapy 
• Other therapy identifies other treatment given that cannot be 
classified as surgery, radiation, systemic therapy, or ancillary
